declared.note: Declared parameters. Not estimated from data. Each is reported to the reader as declared, and each is measurable — see the `measurableBy` field.

strongRecord.reason: Published by an outlet with a strong factual-reporting record, an editorial chain and a corrections policy. Fabrication is rare here and costly when discovered.
strongRecord.measurableBy: a labelled audit of published corrections and retractions per outlet

ordinaryRecord.reason: Published by a rated outlet with an ordinary record.

poorRecord.reason: Published by an outlet our database rates poorly for factual reporting.

unratedOutlet.reason: We hold no reliability record for this publisher. Most unrated outlets are small and legitimate, so this sits well below the rate for an anonymous account.
unratedOutlet.measurableBy: sampling unrated outlets from the feed and labelling them

socialAccount.reason: Posted by an account rather than a publisher: no masthead, no corrections policy, no editorial accountability.
socialAccount.measurableBy: a labelled sample of social posts

corroboration.reason: Note the asymmetry, which is the important part: FINDING independent corroboration is strong evidence a story is genuine, whereas NOT finding it is weak evidence it is fabricated — genuine local and niche reporting is often uncovered elsewhere, and the free news tier indexes a limited set of outlets. That asymmetry is why an uncorroborated article is capped rather than condemned.
corroboration.measurableBy: eval/measureCorroborationRates.js — live feed articles for the genuine row, the adversarial set for the fabricated row

authorControlled.reason: Style, headline wording, attribution and persuasion are all chosen by whoever wrote the text. Their evidence is admitted only in the incriminating direction.
authorControlled.measurableBy: re-estimation on a corpus of competently written fabrications, which would show these ratios approaching 1 on the favourable side

styleWeightCap.reason: Maximum decibans the style family may contribute. Even in the incriminating direction the ISOT ratios are an upper bound, since its fabrications are conspicuously crude; this caps how far one family of correlated, author-controlled signals can move the result.

probabilityBounds.reason: No finite quantity of evidence of this kind justifies certainty, and a reported 0 or 1 would be a claim the system cannot support.

factCheck.reason: How often a claim draws each ruling from a professional desk, given that it is genuine or fabricated. A desk rating a genuine claim false is rare (the rulings are investigated, sourced and corrected when wrong), while a viral fabrication is the desks' main subject, so "rated false" carries a ratio of 60. Absence of a ruling is never entered: desks review a small share of claims.
factCheck.measurableBy: eval/benchmarkCheckAnything.js — the share of known-false and known-true claims for which a matched ruling is found

currentCoverage.reason: Entered only when the news search found the event neither reported nor contradicted. Two independent outlets reporting, this week, things that could not be happening if a claim were true is rare for a genuine claim; the absence rule is guarded to events that would dominate a heavily covered subject, and still weighs less.
currentCoverage.measurableBy: eval/benchmarkCheckAnything.js — the rate at which each outcome fires on known-true and known-false claims

method: per-bin likelihood ratio, Jeffreys-smoothed, shrunk to the conservative end of a 95% interval, reported in decibans (10·log10 LR)

corpus.note: Estimated from the merged writing check (agents/writingChecks.js, WRITING_CHECKS=merged: headline, bias, persuasion and sourcing read in one model call) on the same 239 ISOT articles the four separate checks were measured on (isot_content-only_seed42.jsonl; eval/runEval.js --config content-merged --ids-from), Ollama off, so NIM and Gemini as on the deployed server. Every factor came from the model; none fell back to the pattern check. Held-out validation: eval/results/scoring-validation_merged.json (the separate checks: scoring-validation_separate.json).

style.note: Members correlate, so their summed weight is scaled by `damping` to avoid counting the same evidence several times.

calibration.note: Maps the content-side weight of evidence to a probability. Corroboration evidence is added afterwards in log-odds space, because it is not present in the corpus this map was fitted on.
